2027 Budget second reading passed by 97-vote majority

cards.what_happened: Parliament passed the second reading of the 2027 Budget by a 97-vote majority following a seven-day debate. The vote concluded with 157 votes in favour and 60 votes against. This is the 81st Budget in the history of Sri Lanka.
details: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake presented the proposal on November 12 in his role as Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development. Debate began on November 13 and finished at 6.30 pm on November 20, marking the third budget presented by the National People’s Power government. Records show 157 MPs voted in favour, 60 MPs voted against, and no MPs abstained.

The 2027 Budget estimates total government spending at Rs. 7.933 trillion, up from Rs. 7.309 trillion in revised 2026 estimates. Total revenue is projected at Rs. 6.15 trillion, while revenue and grants reach Rs. 6.18 trillion. These figures leave an estimated budget deficit of Rs. 1.753 trillion, representing 4.5% of Gross Domestic Product.

Alongside these proceedings, Central Bank Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe announced headline inflation will likely exceed 9% this month. In judicial matters, Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama ordered a progress report on the Krrish inquiry by December 01, while MP Chamara Sampath Dassanayake was further remanded until November 27.
key_facts: The 2027 Budget second reading passed with 157 votes in favour and 60 against.
A 97-vote majority cleared the proposal after a seven-day parliamentary debate.
President Anura Kumara Dissanayake presented the proposal on November 12.
Government expenditure is estimated at Rs. 7.933 trillion for 2027.
Total revenue is projected at Rs. 6.15 trillion, creating a Rs. 1.753 trillion deficit.
Committee Stage discussions run from November 21 until December 14 across 19 days.
The final third reading vote is scheduled for 6.00 pm on December 14.
Central Bank Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe expects inflation to top 9% this month.
cards.whats_next: The Committee Stage debate begins on November 21 and runs across 19 days until December 14, meeting at 9.30 am each day except Sundays and public holidays, ahead of a final vote at 6.00 pm on December 14.
cards.blurb: Sri Lanka's Parliament has approved the second reading of the 2027 Budget by a 97-vote majority.
cards.spoken: Sri Lanka's Parliament has approved the second reading of the 2027 Budget by a ninety-seven-vote majority. After seven days of debate, one hundred and fifty-seven lawmakers voted in favour, while sixty voted against, with no abstentions. Presented by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake as Finance Minister, this is the eighty-first budget in the country's history. It outlines government spending of seven point nine three three trillion rupees and projects an estimated deficit of one point seven five three trillion rupees. Meanwhile, Central Bank Governor Dr. Nandalal Weerasinghe warned that inflation will likely top nine percent this month. Lawmakers now move to the Committee Stage debate, which continues until the final vote on December 14.

sri_lanka.title: New court order: Why was BYD banned from selling its new Ti7 SUV in Europe??

cards.what_happened: A Dutch court issued a preliminary injunction on November 20. It blocked BYD from selling its Fang Cheng Bao Ti7 SUV in the European Union. The court found the Ti7 had a similar overall visual impression to the Land Rover Defender and that this infringed design rights.
details: The source is a newswire. BYD, a Chinese electric vehicle giant, got a legal setback. A Dutch court in The Hague issued a preliminary injunction on November 20 after a design rights dispute with British luxury vehicle maker Jaguar Land Rover (JLR).

The court found the BYD Ti7 created a similar overall visual impression to the Land Rover Defender. It cited similarities in overall proportions, rounded shoulders, wheel arches, and window lines. The injunction stopped BYD from importing, manufacturing, offering for sale, selling, storing, or delivering the Ti7 in the European Union.

The restriction applied only to the Ti7 and did not affect BYD’s other vehicles. The Fang Cheng Bao Ti7 is a seven-seat plug-in hybrid SUV from BYD’s Fang Cheng Bao sub-brand. BYD maintained the vehicle was independently designed and did not infringe JLR’s intellectual property rights.

The decision was a legal victory for JLR, which sought to protect the Defender SUV design. But the ruling was a preliminary injunction, not a final judgment after a full trial. The court noted BYD had no concrete plans to bring the Ti7 into the European market at that time, and the case highlights increasing competition as Chinese brands expand.
cards.why_it_matters: The case highlights increasing competition between Chinese automakers and established European manufacturers as Chinese brands continue expanding their international presence.
key_facts: BYD got a legal setback from a Dutch court on November 20.
Preliminary injunction blocked BYD Ti7 in the EU.
Court found Ti7 similar to Land Rover Defender.
JLR sought to protect Defender design rights.
BYD said Ti7 was independently designed.
Court said injunction was not final and no EU plans.
Ti7 is a seven-seat plug-in hybrid SUV.
Case highlights Chinese automaker competition.
cards.blurb: A Dutch court issued a preliminary injunction blocking BYD’s Ti7 SUV in the EU after finding similarities to the Land Rover Defender.
cards.spoken: Here's the scene. A Chinese electric car company called BYD had a legal fight with a British car maker, Jaguar Land Rover. A Dutch court in The Hague gave a ruling on November 20. The court made a preliminary injunction. That blocked BYD from selling its Fang Cheng Bao Ti7 SUV in the European Union. The court said the car had a similar overall visual impression to the Land Rover Defender. It found that was an infringement of design rights. BYD says it was independently designed and does not infringe those rights. JLR says it wanted to protect the Defender design. The order is not a final judgment. The court also said BYD had no concrete plans to bring the Ti7 into the European market then. Here's why it matters. It shows more competition between Chinese automakers and European car makers.

Deadly day on roads: Four killed in Malabe, Mount Lavinia and Eastern Province

cards.what_happened: Four people died in four separate road accidents across Sri Lanka on Friday (20), police said. The dead included a 79-year-old woman from Ratmalana and a 23-year-old motorcyclist from Malwatta 02. The crashes were reported in Malabe, Mount Lavinia, Eravur and Sammanthurai.
details: Police said four people were killed in four different road accidents on Friday (20), in Malabe, Mount Lavinia, Eravur and Sammanthurai. The victims included a 79-year-old woman and a 23-year-old motorcyclist.

In Mount Lavinia, a 79-year-old woman from Ratmalana was hit by a car while she was crossing the Galle–Colombo Road. She was badly injured and taken to Kalubowila Hospital, where she died later. Police arrested the car driver.

On the Batticaloa–Trincomalee Road, a 42-year-old motorcyclist from Manampitiya died in a crash involving several vehicles. Police said a lorry heading towards Valaichchenai hit two motorcycles travelling in front of it, then crashed into a car near the Kattupalli Road junction. Both motorcyclists were badly hurt and taken to Eravur Hospital, where one of them died, and the lorry driver was arrested.

On the Kalmunai–Ampara Road, a 23-year-old motorcyclist from Malwatta 02 died after hitting a lorry coming from the opposite direction; the motorcyclist and the pillion rider were taken to Ampara Hospital with serious injuries, and the rider later died of his injuries. Separately, a pedestrian was struck by a motorcycle running along Wanaguru Mawatha from Horahena Junction towards Hokandara Junction; both were badly hurt and taken to Mulleriyawa Hospital, where the pedestrian died, and police said the pedestrian has not yet been identified. The police stations concerned are still investigating all four accidents.
key_facts: Four people died in four separate road accidents across Sri Lanka on Friday (20), police said.
The crashes were reported in Malabe, Mount Lavinia, Eravur and Sammanthurai.
A 79-year-old woman from Ratmalana died at Kalubowila Hospital after a car hit her in Mount Lavinia.
A 42-year-old motorcyclist from Manampitiya died at Eravur Hospital in a Batticaloa–Trincomalee Road pile-up.
A lorry heading to Valaichchenai hit two motorcycles, then a car near Kattupalli Road junction.
A 23-year-old from Malwatta 02 died at Ampara Hospital after hitting an oncoming lorry.
A pedestrian died at Mulleriyawa Hospital after a motorcycle struck them on Wanaguru Mawatha.
The car and lorry drivers were arrested, the pedestrian is unidentified, and investigations continue.
cards.whats_next: The police stations concerned are continuing investigations into all four accidents, and the identity of the dead pedestrian has not yet been established.
cards.blurb: Four people died in four separate road crashes across Sri Lanka on Friday, including a 79-year-old woman and two motorcyclists.
cards.spoken: Police in Sri Lanka are reporting a deadly day on the roads. Four people lost their lives in four separate accidents on Friday the twentieth. The crashes were reported from Malabe, Mount Lavinia, Eravur and Sammanthurai. In Mount Lavinia, a seventy-nine year old woman from Ratmalana was crossing the Galle to Colombo Road when a car struck her. She died at Kalubowila Hospital, and the driver was arrested. On the Batticaloa to Trincomalee Road, a lorry heading towards Valaichchenai ran into two motorcycles and then a car near the Kattupalli Road junction. A forty-two year old rider from Manampitiya died at Eravur Hospital, and the lorry driver was arrested. A twenty-three year old from Malwatta zero two died at Ampara Hospital after hitting an oncoming lorry. And a pedestrian, still unidentified, died at Mulleriyawa Hospital after a motorcycle struck them. Police are investigating all four.

Appeal Court stresses need to protect elephants as national heritage

cards.what_happened: The Court of Appeal emphasised that elephants must be safeguarded as a vital national resource and heritage. The bench made this observation while hearing a legal challenge against a government policy permitting firearms for farmers. The court noted that international tourists visit Sri Lanka to see wildlife rather than large buildings.
details: The Sri Lanka Wildlife and Nature Protection Society filed a petition asking the court to overturn the government's decision to issue guns to farmers for crop protection. The case was heard on Tuesday by Court of Appeal President Justice Rohitha Abeysuriya and Justice Priyantha Fernando. The petitioner's lawyer, President's Counsel Sanjeewa Jayawardena, warned that giving firearms to farmers seriously imperils wild animals, especially elephants, noting that the tusker Kawanthissa had already been shot dead.

Jayawardena informed the judges that the minimum landholding required to obtain a firearm had recently been reduced by the government from five acres to two acres, which could lead to many more weapons being handed out. He revealed that 305 firearms were distributed by 2002, 490 by 2026, and data indicated a total of 3,207 firearms have been issued so far.

Justice Abeysuriya stated that the court places significant weight on protecting the environment and wildlife, stressing that elephants are a national asset and that tourists do not travel to the island for tall buildings. The court said it would seek proposals from all parties on ways to keep elephants safe. Named respondents include Deputy Defence Minister retired Major General Aruna Jayasekara, Defence Ministry Secretary Air Vice Marshal Sampath Thuyacontha, and Environment Minister Dr. Dammika Patabendi.
cards.why_it_matters: The case highlights concerns that loosening rules on issuing firearms to farmers puts endangered wildlife, particularly the national elephant population, at severe risk.
key_facts: The Court of Appeal considered a petition against issuing firearms to farmers to guard crops.
Court President Justice Rohitha Abeysuriya said foreign tourists visit for nature, not large buildings.
The land eligibility threshold for getting a firearm was lowered from five acres to two acres.
Lawyer Sanjeewa Jayawardena noted that 3,207 firearms have reportedly been issued so far.
Firearm totals reached 305 by 2002 and 490 by 2026.
The petitioner highlighted the fatal shooting of the tusker Kawanthissa.
Court adjourned the matter until November 30 to seek safety proposals.
cards.whats_next: The Court of Appeal will obtain submissions from all parties on measures to safeguard elephants and will continue hearing the petition on November 30.
cards.blurb: Sri Lanka's Court of Appeal has called for elephant protection, saying tourists visit for wildlife, not large buildings.
cards.spoken: Sri Lanka's Court of Appeal has stepped in to stress the vital importance of protecting the nation's wild elephants. While hearing a legal challenge against a government decision to hand out firearms to farmers, Court President Justice Rohitha Abeysuriya remarked that foreign tourists come to Sri Lanka to experience its natural heritage, not to look at large buildings. The court heard that authorities lowered the land size needed to get a gun from five acres down to two, and over three thousand firearms have already been distributed. With animals like the tusker Kawanthissa recently shot dead, wildlife advocates want the policy scrapped. The judges will collect safety ideas from all sides and resume hearings on November 30.

Poland says Russian missile hit its territory during attack on Ukraine

cards.what_happened: Russia launched a major overnight attack on Ukraine, firing ballistic missiles at bridges in Kyiv and railway stations across the country. The strikes hit key crossings in the capital and left at least nine people dead. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called it one of the most massive strikes of the war so far.
details: Russia launched a major overnight attack across Ukraine, targeting bridges in Kyiv and railway stations with ballistic missiles. Key crossings in the capital were hit during the nationwide assault. At least nine people were killed.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky described the strike as one of the most massive of the war so far. The attack came days after Ukraine badly damaged the strategically important Crimean Bridge. Russian President Vladimir Putin had threatened to retaliate for that earlier attack on the bridge.

The Kremlin built the Crimean Bridge to link Russia and the occupied peninsula. The latest strikes took place during a flurry of talks about the war. They also came as the Kremlin pushed back against a US claim that Russia could be open to Western-backed security guarantees for Ukraine.
BBC reporter Sarah Rainsford was in Kyiv after the night of strikes to report on what happened.
key_facts: Russia attacked bridges in Kyiv and railway stations overnight with ballistic missiles.
At least nine people were killed in the nationwide assault on Ukraine.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called it one of the war's most massive strikes.
The attack came days after Ukraine damaged the strategically important Crimean Bridge.
Vladimir Putin had threatened to retaliate for the Crimean Bridge attack.
The Kremlin built the bridge to link Russia and the occupied peninsula.
Strikes happened during talks about the war and after a US claim on security guarantees.
BBC reporter Sarah Rainsford was in Kyiv after the strikes.
cards.blurb: Russia launched a massive overnight missile attack on Kyiv and across Ukraine, killing at least nine people.
cards.spoken: Hello and welcome. Russia has launched a major overnight attack on Ukraine, firing ballistic missiles at bridges in Kyiv and railway stations across the country. At least nine people were killed. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called it one of the most massive strikes of the war so far. The assault came just days after Ukraine damaged the strategically important Crimean Bridge, which Russia built to link itself with the occupied peninsula. Vladimir Putin had previously threatened to retaliate for that bridge attack. The strikes also happened while there was a flurry of talks about the war, and as Russia pushed back against a US claim that it might accept Western-backed security guarantees for Ukraine. BBC reporter Sarah Rainsford was in Kyiv after the strikes to bring us the latest.
